# Daily Development Update: hCurators Manual Curation Feature and hSnaps Fixes

## hCurators

### Add Missing Item Feature for Curators and Admins

- Curators and admins now have a new "Add Missing Item" menu option in the sidebar.
- Sometimes the system misses posts or comments because Hive servers lag behind — this feature lets curators manually add those missed items.
- Curators simply paste the URL of the missed post/comment and hit submit.
- The system checks if the item is valid, fetches its details from Hive, and adds it to the curation queue.
- If an item was previously rejected, submitting it again will restore it back to pending.
- Flagged authors are still blocked — their content cannot be added.
- Everything works the same way as if the system had caught the item automatically.

In the HIVE ecosystem, we can evaluate a witness from many dimensions: community reputation, historical contributions, activity level… but ultimately, **the most important factor is just one thing — whether they are running a stable node that consistently produces blocks.**


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyr9BUEhswgJ5aBD1BAo9T48qdiYXxW7mEaCGpprvpyo/image.png)


If a witness node is running an outdated version for a long time, producing delayed or stalled blocks, or frequently going offline, then regardless of their past contributions or reputation, it may be time to reconsider your vote.

The problem is:  
👉 For most users, **evaluating node health and reviewing their votes is not an easy task.**

Although we previously introduced a witness list tool (https://www.cutehive.com/witnesses) to simplify this process, it still lacks intuitive clarity for fast decision-making.

---

## 🧭 Hive Witness Monitor: Turning Complexity into Clarity

That’s why we built a new tool:

## 🚀 Hive Witness Monitor

Its goal is simple:  
👉 **Make witness evaluation and vote checking effortless, intuitive, and even enjoyable.**

---

## ✨ Why Do You Need It?

In HIVE’s decentralized world, **witnesses are the backbone of consensus**.  
As a stakeholder, every vote you cast directly impacts the network’s security and future.

But in reality:

- There are hundreds of witnesses  
- Node status changes frequently  
- Traditional lists are not intuitive enough  

👉 This is exactly the problem Hive Witness Monitor is designed to solve.


![8d829f5df67dbc5a1ff24336a5b8ae3d.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTApEqCVBh8i8y6FCFGP2kK3aCVifV1W7vhL2fmaTxdfX/8d829f5df67dbc5a1ff24336a5b8ae3d.png)


## 🔍 Key Features

### ✅ Instantly Understand Node Health

We use multi-dimensional data analysis to classify witnesses intelligently:

result.body:
In the last post I described our communication system ([czat i prywatne wiadomości](/hive-139531/@sarmatia.app/public-chat-and-private-dm-made-only-on-blokchain)). After publishing it, I had a very interesting exchange with @gtg, as a result of which I added a warning to the messages: if you lose your memo key, a thief will gain access to the entire message history. Therefore, this system should only be used for non-sensitive communication (the app is meant to be a kind of game, so in principle, no one should even think of sending sensitive messages there anyway). I also added online activity indicators so users know who is currently online. In the plans: adding a blacklist to the inbox and other convenience features.

Today, however, I’ll show you the next important stage in the development of our app — the **Missions module**.

### Types of Missions

Missions can be extremely varied, and I’m sure I haven’t foreseen all the possibilities (there will be room for app updates :)). Still, I tried to include the options that seemed most important to me.

First and foremost — the **reward** issue. The app currently supports 3 types of rewards:

- **Barter**: A descriptive reward with no payment guarantee, but a simple rating system for the mission issuer is provided. The account that took on the mission, completed it, and received acceptance of completion will be able to give a simple note: whether the issuer fulfilled the payment or not.
- **Tokens**: Both native ones (HIVE, HBD) and those from Hive Engine. Payment is guaranteed through a mechanism similar to a smart-contract escrow (a trusted intermediary — the app’s account).
- **Merit Points**: Points that will be used to create rankings and more within the game layer of the app. Only admins can award these.

What else can we set?

- How many people can take on a given mission. In the case of a token reward, this must be a finite number; in the case of barter, it can be unlimited. We can also add exclusions so that selected people cannot take on the mission.
- We can set the duration of the announcement. This is useful because sometimes completing a mission after a certain date no longer makes sense…
- We also have to set the time within which we declare we will review the correct completion of the mission.
- The final element is an optional pin on the map. The map will be an important part of our app, so we can, for example, commission an article about a battle that took place in a specific location. Such a mission will be visible both on the list and on the map.

Adding options looks like this:  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/23sweHStVBtdi8uneuDEsmZmGyaD37hPTUdpqSjvrQfB8AQKyBoFSKk7u7JFtmNNvbL3R.png)

### Process

I consider the proper process to be the most important thing in this kind of system, so that it provides maximum fairness and transparency. That’s why completing a mission in our app can be a multi-stage process.

The first step is, of course, creating the mission. Any logged-in user can do this, although the admin has a few extra options. The mission itself is a post on the blockchain. All additional mission attributes are stored in the post’s json_metadata. After publication, the mission appears on the list:  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/23t76k7pL8Qj18YdJvJykyNz4bJDWu8FAHJvdsCvtwznkzxghumDkzttRsFny6vuMCJWx.png)

The next step is, naturally, accepting the mission by a user. If the mission was intended for single use or the last available slot has been taken, it becomes locked for other users after acceptance. After completing the mission, you go into it in the app, click the “Report Completion” button, then enter a descriptive justification and/or a link. And you wait for the issuer’s approval:  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/EnynaEEWj1nG6ekmLJu75Pi71Rr9bZK9HUZZon2YQwCcaJdSHMty2fyjzm8NxQmc6kU.png)

At this point, there are two paths. Either the issuer accepts it — and then the token reward is automatically sent to the person who completed the mission (or the issuer makes the barter payment). Or the work is rejected (optionally with a justification).

However, that’s not the end, because the person who completed the mission can either accept the “verdict” or appeal it. In the appeal, they can also add a justification.

The appeal is resolved by an admin, who can either side with the person who completed the mission (in which case the automatic payout occurs, or the issuer is honor-bound to do what they committed to — if they don’t, they receive a negative rating) or side with the issuer. And that concludes the mission process.

Every subsequent step is recorded in the comments under the mission post, so the entire course is fully transparent.

### Adding a Mission vs. the Hive Feed

As mentioned, a mission is a post, so it also has the standard text editor, title, tags, and beneficiaries. Due to the nature of this post, we added an automatic system that sets the @null account as the default beneficiary (though it can be removed). Sometimes the mission itself can be valuable content worthy of upvotes and a Hive community reward. However, we added one more feature — internal tags. This solution allows good filtering on the mission list on one hand, while on the other it prevents cluttering the actual post tags if the mission doesn’t need wider publication or if it would be closer to spam than valuable content.

### Statistics

Statistics are a nice thing — I like them. That’s why we added a tab on the user’s account where they can check the history of both missions they’ve taken on and those they’ve commissioned. When you open them, you’ll see the full history of the mission process.  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/23swfvnJUfidJCD3NSNcYUMcvtgxthK6w5oz5SF3EC4DHcssvvBCMijE3YCpCijyK19gW.png)

The history is saved to an off-chain database so we don’t have to query the blockchain every single time.

And that’s all for today. I hope you like the mission system — feel free to share your thoughts in the comments :)

---
## Moduł Misji w Sarmatiamundi

W ostatnim poście opisałem nasz system komunikacji ([czat i prywatne wiadomości](/hive-139531/@sarmatia.app/public-chat-and-private-dm-made-only-on-blokchain)). Po publikacji odbyłem bardzo ciekawą wymianę zdań z @gtg w efekcie czego dodałem ostrzeżenie przy wiadomościach iż w wypadku utraty klucza memo, złodziej będzie miał dostęp do całej historii wiadomości, więc można używać tego systemu tylko do niewrażliwej komunikacji (aplikacja ma być swego rodzaju grą, więc co do zasady raczej nikt nawet nie będzie miał pomysłu by przesyłać tam wiadomości wrażliwych). Dodałem także oznaczenia o aktywności, by użytkownicy wiedzieli kto jest on-line. W planie dodanie do skrzynki blacklisty i inne ułatwienia.

Dziś natomiast pokażę kolejny ważny etap tworzenia naszej aplikacji, a więc moduł Misji.

### Rodzaje misji

Misje mogą być różne, najróżniejsze i z pewnością masy możliwości nie przewidziałem (będzie miejsce na aktualizacje aplikacji :)) ale postarałem się dodać opcje które wydały mi się najważniejsze. 
Przede wszystkim kwestia nagroda. Aplikacja dopuszcza obecnie 3 rodzaje nagrody:
- Barter: nagroda w formie opisowej, brak gwarancji wypłaty, ale przewidziany jest prosty system oceny zlecającego misję (konto które się podjęło misji, wykonało, dostało akcept wykonania będzie mogło dać prostą informację: zlecający wywiązał się lub nie wywiązał z wypłąty)
- Tokeny: zarówno natywne (HIVE, HBD), jak i te z Hive Engine. Gwarancja realizacji zapłaty poprzez mechanizm jak w smart-contract escrow (zaufany pośrednik - konto aplikacji)
- Punkty Zasług: Punkty, które będą służyć do tworzenia rankingu i nie tylko w warstwie grywalnej aplikacji, te mogą przyznawać tylko admini.

A co jeszcze możemy ustawić?
- ile osób może się podjąć danej misji, w przypadku nagrody w formie tokenowej musi to być skończona ilość, w przypadku barteru może być nieskończona. Możemy też dodać wykluczenia, tak aby wybrane przez nas osoby nie mogły podjąć się misji.
- możemy również ustawić czas trwania ogłoszenia. To przydatne, bo czasami wykonanie misji po jakiejś dacie przestaje mieć sens...
- musimy także ustawić czas, w jakim deklarujemy rozpatrzenie prawidłowego wykonania misji.
- ostatnim wreszcie elementem jest opcjonalna pinezka. Mapa będzie ważnym elementem naszej aplikacji, dlatego możemy zlecić np napisanie artykułu o bitwie która odbyła się w jakimś konkretnym miejscu. Taka misja będzie widoczna zarówno na liście jak i na mapie. 

Dodawanie opcji wygląda tak:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/23sweHStVBtdi8uneuDEsmZmGyaD37hPTUdpqSjvrQfB8AQKyBoFSKk7u7JFtmNNvbL3R.png)


### Proces

Za najważniejsze w tego typu systemie uważam właściwy proces tak aby zapewniał maksimum uczciwości i przejrzystości. Dlatego też przebieg wypełniania misji w naszej aplikacji może być wieloetapowy.
Pierwszym krokiem jest oczywiście ustanowienie misji. Może to zrobić każdy zalogowany użytkownik chociaż admin ma trochę dodatkowych opcji. Sama misja jest postem na blokchainie. Wszystkie dodatkowe atrybuty misji są w json_metadata postu. Po publikacji misja pojawia się na liście:

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/23t76k7pL8Qj18YdJvJykyNz4bJDWu8FAHJvdsCvtwznkzxghumDkzttRsFny6vuMCJWx.png)

Kolejnym krokiem, jest oczywiście przyjęcie misji przez użytkownika. Jeśli misja była przeznaczona do jednorazowego użycia, lub zostało ostatnie użycie, po podjęciu misji jest ona zablokowana dla innych użytkowników. Po wykonaniu misji, wchodzimy w nią w aplikacji klikamy guziczek zgłoś wykonanie i następnie wpisujemy uzasadnienie opisowe i/lub link. I czekamy na akceptacje zlecającego:

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/EnynaEEWj1nG6ekmLJu75Pi71Rr9bZK9HUZZon2YQwCcaJdSHMty2fyjzm8NxQmc6kU.png)

I teraz mamy dwie ścieżki. Albo zlecający akceptuje i wtedy nagroda tokenowa automatycznie idzie do wykonującego misję, lub zlecający wykonuje inną zapłate (barterową). Albo następuje odrzucenie pracy (opcjonalnie z uzasadnieniem.

To jednak nie koniec, bo wykonujący może albo przyjąć "werdykt" albo się odwołać. Przy odwołaniu również może dodać uzasadnienie.
Rozstrzygającym odwołanie jest admin i może on albo przyznać rację wykonującemu (i wtedy następuje wypłata automatyczna, lub zleceniodawca jest zobowiązany honorem aby zrobić to do czego się zobowiązał - jeśli nie zrobi dostanie negatywną ocenę) albo zlecającemu. I na tym kończy się proces przebiegu misji.
Każdy kolejny krok jest zapisywany w komentarzach do postu-misji, więc przebieg jest w pełni transparentny.

### Dodawanie misji, a feed hive
Misja jak było to wspomniane jest postem, więc ma też standardowy edytor tekstu, tytuł, tagi, beneficjenci. Ze względu na charakter tego postu dodaliśmy automat ustanawiający konto @null jako domyślny beneficjent (ale można go usunąć). Czasem misja sama w sobie może być wartościową treścią godną upvotów i nagrody społeczności hive. Dodaliśmy jednak jeszcze jeden dodatek - tagi wewnętrzne. Takie rozwiązanie ma z jednej strony umożliwić dobre filtrowanie na liście misji, a z drugiej nie zaśmiecać tagów z faktycznymi postami, jeśli misja nie wymaga by ją gdzieś szerzej publikować, czy miałaby charakter bliższy spamowi niż wartościowej treści.

### Statystyki

Statystyki to fajna rzecz, ja ją lubię. Dlatego dodaliśmy na koncie użytkownika zakładke gdzie może sprawdzić historię zarówno podjętych misji jak i zleconych, a wchodząc w nie będzie widział historię procesu misji. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sarmatia.app/23swfvnJUfidJCD3NSNcYUMcvtgxthK6w5oz5SF3EC4DHcssvvBCMijE3YCpCijyK19gW.png)
Historia, zapisuje się do bazy of-chain, żeby nie trzeba było za każdym razem odpytywać blokchainu. 
No i to tyle na dziś, mam nadzieję, że system misji się Wam podoba, podzielcie się refleksjami w komentarzu :)

I do not like making claims without evidence. Today, instead of asking you to trust my words, I am sharing our actual server analytics directly from Cloudflare, the infrastructure layer that supports hivepostify.cloud.


![pp24](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/243c011939fd9badf9207caefc75aba8.webp)


Every number below comes from our live Cloudflare dashboard. Nothing is exaggerated. Nothing is estimated. This is what is happening on this platform right now.

---

## Traffic Overview - Previous 7 Days

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total Requests | 1,750,000 |
| Cached Requests | 14,230 |
| Uncached Requests | 1,740,000 |
| Total Bandwidth | 20.46 GB |
| Cached Bandwidth | 9.66 GB |
| Uncached Bandwidth | 10.80 GB |

In the last seven days, our servers handled one million seven hundred and fifty thousand requests. Over twenty gigabytes of data served real users loading real pages, real images, and real content from Hive worldwide.



![2](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/c18424baa56d81b41733b1e30c703a72.webp)


![3](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/90c578da4d026159e8dd89d3c584cc1b.webp)


![4](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/114104896514751be36454581e8eb14b.webp)

*These Images are 24 Hours Data*



The fact that 1,740,000 out of 1,750,000 requests are uncached and hitting our origin server directly indicates something important. Most of our traffic consists of dynamic, live, and personalized content. This includes logged-in users, API responses, and real-time Hive blockchain data. This is what an active social platform looks like, not a static landing page with inflated numbers.

---

## Unique Visitors - Previous 7 Days

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total Unique Visitors | 9,140 |
| Peak Day (Maximum) | 2,440 visitors |
| Lowest Day (Minimum) | 309 visitors |




Over nine thousand unique people visited hivepostify.cloud in the past seven days. The growth trend between our minimum and maximum day shows that the platform is gaining momentum, not losing it.

---

## Top Traffic Countries - Previous 24 Hours

| Country | Requests |
|---|---|
| United States | 189,295 |
| Pakistan | 25,520 |
| France | 3,833 |
| Switzerland | 86 |
| Netherlands | 58 |





![5](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/f82253b407d7bd2b0df11bbd25c4f4e4.webp)


![6](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/92e437275997d196e12dc420ab9aa001.webp)

 


The United States leading our traffic is a significant point in this report. HivePostify is not just a local Pakistani platform; it is also being discovered and used by international audiences. American users reading content on a platform created by a student in Pakistan on the Hive blockchain indicates real product quality and content worth engaging.

Pakistan is our second largest source, which aligns with our mission. Our active Facebook ad campaigns targeting Pakistani freelancers and content creators are clearly converting into real visits.

---

## HTTP Version Distribution - Previous 24 Hours

| Protocol | Requests | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP/1.1 | 196,006 | 86.72% |
| HTTP/2 | 15,546 | 6.88% |
| HTTP/3 | 14,479 | 6.41% |



![7](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/e2d7e33d47972ebe3947fb7a34ba08dc.webp)
 

The presence of HTTP/3 traffic means modern clients are successfully negotiating our fastest available protocol. This indicates our server configuration is optimized for performance.

---

## Content Type Breakdown - Previous 24 Hours

| Content Type | Requests | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| JSON | 192,854 | 88.06% |
| HTML | 16,075 | 7.34% |
| Empty | 8,922 | 4.07% |
| TXT | 579 | 0.30% |
| JS | 150 | 0.07% |
| PNG | 131 | 0.06% |
| CSS | 109 | 0.05% |
| WebP | 102 | 0.05% |
| Other | 72 | 0.03% |



![8](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/d28dc16816c7c2cc5653a95d3d6f5b2e.webp)
 


This table is the most important one in this entire post for anyone who understands how web applications work.

88.06% of all our traffic returns JSON data. JSON responses are API calls, which represent users actively engaging with the platform. This includes loading feeds, submitting posts, retrieving blockchain data, placing orders on the marketplace, and voting on content.

A platform where nearly 90% of traffic is live API activity indicates that people are not just visiting; they are using it.

---

## Bandwidth Saved by Caching - Previous 24 Hours

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total Bandwidth | 1.58 GB |
| Saved by Cache | 261.29 MB |
| Cache Saving Percentage | 17% |



![9](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/9d49172973717ae8f0fd1f27564fd959.webp)
 


Cloudflare's caching layer saved us 264 megabytes in a single day. This helps keep our infrastructure costs down and improves load times for users everywhere.

---

## Core Web Vitals - Page Load Performance

| LCP Score | Percentage of Visits |
|---|---|
| Good | 57% |
| Needs Improvement | 11% |
| Poor | 31% |

| LCP Percentile | Load Time |
|---|---|
| P50 (Median) | 1,832ms |
| P75 | 4,580ms |
| P90 | 6,620ms |
| P99 | 17,716ms |




![10](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/244806f092587d49dc520add51730397.webp)

*Latest On Track*
 


**Average Page Load Time: 880ms**

I am sharing this openly because I believe in full transparency, not just when the numbers look good.

The Poor percentage is real, and we know exactly why it happens. Posts containing images hosted on third-party services, like PeakD, can show LCP times as high as 15 seconds. These images are embedded in content created by Hive users across the ecosystem, and we have no control over their hosting speeds.

Our self-hosted images tell a different story. One of our WebP-compressed images in the debug data shows an LCP of just 3.1 seconds, which is significantly better and within an acceptable range for a live blockchain application making real-time API calls.

We are actively working on lazy loading and image optimization to reduce the Poor percentage. This is part of our roadmap, and we will fix it.

The 880ms average load time across all visits is a strong result for any platform making live Hive blockchain calls and rendering decentralized content in real time.

---

![11](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/f9c1701acd3a9a6f3660b60d562be73c.webp)


![12](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/280a1db3b151a8431d06bf712a27385c.webp)


![13](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/22a728021ce850348e694c5492962f05.webp)


![14](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/5958ba9861c21b7d4c53771fc1e8adab.webp)
 
 
 
 





## What This Data Means for Hive

Here is a simple summary of everything above.

In the last seven days, over nine thousand unique people visited a Hive-powered platform. 1.75 million requests were handled by our servers. Twenty gigabytes of Hive content was served to users in the United States, Pakistan, France, and beyond.



![14](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/d17f46029ef52a82ef4c594dc6db08b7.webp)

*24 Hours*
 

![15](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/e30a339d71b143f5e2914a50bf1e34ab.webp)

*30 Days Data*
 


This is not a proposal or a roadmap. This is a live report of what is happening right now.

HivePostify is driving real international traffic to Hive content. Every article read on our platform is part of the Hive ecosystem being engaged by someone who may never have discovered it through hive.blog or PeakD. Every Pakistani freelancer who visits our marketplace is a potential new Hive account. Every local user who finds out they can withdraw to EasyPaisa or JazzCash is a user who's likely to stay long-term.

All of this is happening without any DHF funding, without a team, and without outside investment.

---

## What We Still Need

The data shows the platform works. But two factors are stopping us from converting this traffic into long-term Hive users.

We need delegated HP at @hivepostify. New users who post their first content require votes to stay. Without that signal, they leave within a week. Each HP delegation directly boosts user retention.

#### Upvote this post. 
Every reward goes to account claims and server costs.

#### Delegate to @hivepostify.
 Your HP stays yours. You can withdraw it anytime. While delegated, it helps keep new users active on Hive.

---

**Today, I want to share something** I've been quietly working on. It’s not live yet; we're 95% finished. However, I believe this community deserves to know where HivePostify is headed before we launch.


![p35252](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/488a62e67fc1d7b324b8151c2c7ce880.webp)




## The Problem I Kept Thinking About

Right now, every creator on Hive publishes everything to everyone. There is no middle ground. You either make your work available to everyone for free, or you don’t publish it at all.

That works for most content. But what about the creator who has spent years developing real expertise? What about the writer whose in-depth research posts take 12 hours to create? What about the photographer, analyst, educator, or strategist?

They deserve more than a 7-day payout window and a public post that anyone can access forever without contributing a single token.

I am creating a solution.


## What I Am Building: Exclusive Content on HivePostify

This idea is not vague. The work is already underway. Here is exactly what the system will look like.

Creators can mark any content as exclusive.  This includes articles, long-form posts, in-depth guides, and premium material. The content gets published, but the full content is locked.

Every exclusive post gets a public preview. Anyone browsing HivePostify can see the title, an introduction, and enough context to understand what it’s about. It’s like a trailer; it shows what’s inside without revealing everything. The post link will be on the Hive blockchain, as always, but the full content will be securely stored in the HivePostify database.

#### Access works two ways, and I am still deciding which to choose:
The first option is pay-per-post. A reader finds a post they want, pays a one-time amount set by the creator, and permanently unlocks that specific post. Simple and straightforward, with no commitment needed.

The second option is subscriptions. A reader subscribes to a creator, gaining access to all that creator's exclusive content as long as their subscription is active. One payment gives full library access.

My instinct is to launch with pay-per-post first. It lowers the barrier for both sides. Readers won’t have to commit to a monthly payment before even reading a piece. Once trust is established, the subscription option can be added later.


![1](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/181a17a17ef1cec3f2343670f6cc5685.webp)
 

![2](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/ce7ded57c9446323a4cf4f1d891a38ef.webp)
 

But I genuinely want to hear what this community thinks. I will explain more about why at the end.



## The Creator Is in Control. Completely.

This is crucial, and I want to be clear.

HivePostify does not set prices; I do not set prices. The creator decides the price for every single piece of content and for every subscription tier they choose to offer.

If you want to charge 2 HIVE for a detailed analysis post, that’s your decision. If you want to offer a monthly subscription at 15 HIVE, that’s up to you. The platform facilitates the transaction while giving the creator control.

Payments will be accepted in HIVE and AHPT, the native utility token of HivePostify. I don't plan to add HBD at launch. Eventually, Hive Engine tokens may be included, but I want to keep things focused and stable for now.

#### What does HivePostify take?

I’ve been considering this and think it will be between 0.01% and 11.3% per transaction. I haven’t finalized that number yet. I’m seeking real feedback before making a decision, aiming for fairness to creators and sustainability for the platform.


![3](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/fea7e0a85fe16e14a1f96d805260c888.webp)
 



## The Writing Experience Is Not Hive Markdown

This matters a lot to me.

Standard Hive markdown is functional, but it doesn’t provide the experience I want for exclusive content creators. When someone is creating premium content on HivePostify, the editor should reflect the quality of their work.

The exclusive content editor will have better formatting tools than standard markdown offers. It will allow richer layouts and give more control over how a piece looks when read. This should create an experience that feels worth paying for before the reader even sees the first line.

Details about the editor are still being refined, but this is a key part of the plan.



## What This Means for the Hive Ecosystem

Every paid access on the exclusive content system brings new value to Hive. A reader pays HIVE or AHPT to unlock a post. That HIVE comes from outside the creator's current earnings. It’s new money entering the chain.


![4](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/8c6caba89d64dacfd9c54bb8be1369d7.webp)
 

Creators who build real audiences will have a steady income stream that doesn’t expire after seven days. This gives creators a reason to invest seriously in Hive rather than treating it as a secondary platform.

My board exams are approaching, which means progress will slow down for a bit. I want to be honest about that rather than go quiet and leave people wondering. Development will continue. Nothing is being put on hold. The moment my exams are behind me, we will move forward at full speed.



## I Need Your Honest Opinion

Before I finalize the structure, I have two genuine questions for anyone who has read this far.

#### Should exclusive content launch with pay-per-post, monthly subscriptions, or both?

#### And a tougher one: What percentage cut is fair for HivePostify to take per transaction?

I’m not asking these questions just as a formality. The answers will directly influence what gets built. If the community strongly prefers subscriptions from day one, I will make that happen. If there is a specific number that feels right for platform fees, I want to hear it before deciding in private.

This community has been with HivePostify since the beginning. You deserve a say before we launch.

The platform is live at hivepostify.cloud.

Built on Hive. One student. One mission. Still building.

Last week Anthropic quietly dropped a report on a model called Mythos. The short version is that it found thousands of zero day vulnerabilities across every major operating system and every major web browser.

One of those bugs was 27 years old. It lived in OpenBSD. Yes, OpenBSD. The operating system famous for having the most paranoid security review process in the industry.

That bug survived decades of human review, millions of automated fuzzing runs, and an entire cottage industry of people who do nothing but look for BSD vulnerabilities for a living. Mythos found it on a prompt that essentially amounted to please find a security vulnerability in this program.

Think about that for a second. Then think about the code running your favourite blockchain.

## What Mythos actually does

Mythos is not a security specific model. It is a general purpose frontier model that happens to be terrifyingly good at cyber work. Anthropic restricted access to a handpicked group of partners under something called Project Glasswing. The public does not get it. Very few defenders do either.

The numbers from the red team report are the part that should get everyone's attention. Over 83 percent success rate on reproducing vulnerabilities and developing working exploits on the first attempt. Going from a CVE identifier and a git commit hash to a full working exploit chain in under a day, for under 2000 USD in compute.

Multi vulnerability privilege escalation chains in the Linux kernel. JIT heap sprays escaping browser sandboxes. A remote code execution exploit against FreeBSD that Mythos wrote autonomously. A 16 year old bug in FFmpeg. A 27 year old bug in OpenBSD. And critically, over 99 percent of what they found has not yet been patched.

Mythos is not an incremental improvement on existing vulnerability scanners. It sits in a different category of tool.

## OpenAI is playing catch up and they know it

Within a week of Mythos being announced, OpenAI shipped GPT-5.4-Cyber to their Trusted Access for Cyber program. It is a variant of GPT-5.4 fine tuned specifically for defensive security work, with a lower refusal boundary for legitimate security queries. It also introduces binary reverse engineering capabilities, letting security professionals analyse compiled software without access to source code.

OpenAI also has a separate cyber product that Axios reported on. That product is different from OpenAI's upcoming model Spud, and the cyber capabilities of Spud itself are unclear.

Spud is the internal codename for what is widely expected to be GPT-6. Pre training for the next generation architecture reportedly concluded in late March 2026. A leaked internal memo describes Spud as an important step in the intelligence foundation for the next generation of work, with early customer feedback pointing to stronger reasoning and more reliable production results. Nobody outside OpenAI knows what its cyber capabilities look like, but given the trajectory of every previous GPT release it is safe to assume Spud will push past Mythos in at least some domains.

The pattern is clear. Frontier labs are gating their most capable models because they are genuinely afraid of what will happen when these capabilities are in the hands of people who want to burn things down. We are in the era of AI models being too dangerous to release, which is the exact framing OpenAI used for GPT-2 back in 2019. GPT-2 turned out to be laughably tame. This time they might actually be right.

## The uncomfortable part for crypto

Legacy codebases are where the real horror is. Mythos did not find those OpenBSD and FFmpeg bugs because it got clever. It found them because there were decades of accumulated assumptions nobody had questioned since the code was written.

Blockchain code is legacy code. Even when it is new.

Bitcoin's codebase is old. Ethereum's clients are old. Hive's core is a fork of the BitShares Graphene codebase that dates back to 2015. That is 11 years of assumptions baked into C++ that was designed when most of us were still using Bootstrap 3.

Now ask yourself how many people have actually sat down and done a serious security review of the Hive core in the last five years. Not a witness skimming a PR. Not a bounty hunter chasing a specific class of bug. A proper, paid, methodical review of the signing code, the consensus logic, the RC system, the resource math, the plugin surface area. As far as I know the answer at the protocol level is essentially zero. I know the core of Hive is in very capable hands, but if it can happen to OpenBSD it can happen to anyone.

## Where Hive actually sits

Let me be specific because this matters. Hive is a Graphene chain, meaning the layer 1 is written in C++ with a fairly narrow operation set. No general purpose smart contracts at layer 1. That is genuinely a security advantage because the attack surface is smaller than an EVM chain. Fewer moving parts, fewer sharp edges.

But Hive is not just the layer 1. There is Hive Engine, the JavaScript side chain running custom tokens worth real money and an entire DeFi ecosystem on top. Hive Engine is a Node.js based solution. There is Magi which opens Hive up to other blockxhains, smart contracts and so on. A lot of projects are working on their own EVM integrations. There are half a dozen frontends, each with their own auth flow, each integrating with Keychain or HiveAuth.

Every one of those is attack surface. Every one of those is written in languages Mythos and Spud understand extremely well. Every one of those has probably never been properly audited.

The Hive MetaMask Snap got a Hacken audit last year. That is good. That is one component of one integration. The actual chain code, the layer 2s, the signing libraries, the frontends, the bridges, none of that has been through a comparable process as far as I can tell.

## What happens when Spud is public

Right now the frontier cyber capable models are gated. Mythos is only accessible through Project Glasswing. GPT-5.4-Cyber requires TAC verification. Spud has not shipped.

This will not last. It never does.

Open weights models are catching up fast. AISLE published a test where small open source models, some with only around 3.6 billion active parameters at eleven cents per million tokens, detected Mythos's flagship FreeBSD exploit. A 5.1 billion active parameter open model recovered the core chain of the 27 year old OpenBSD bug. The gap between frontier and open is narrowing, not widening.

Within 12 months you will be able to run something Mythos adjacent on a rented H100. Within 24 months you will probably run it on your own hardware. At that point the people prompting it are not going to be ArmorCode customers. They will be the same people already picking at Hive Engine token contracts looking for a payday.

## The DHF elephant in the room

Hive has a Decentralised Hive Fund. It pays out hundreds of thousands of HIVE a month to proposals. Most of that goes to community building, tooling, marketing, and a lot of ValuePlan shaped holes that the community has been arguing about for months.

You know what has never been funded at any meaningful scale? A comprehensive security review of the Hive core codebase.

We spend on frontends. We spend on games. We spend on marketing campaigns that go nowhere. We do not spend on the thing that, if it fails, kills the entire chain instantly and irrecoverably.

This is not a hypothetical. Poly Network was 611 million USD gone. Ronin was 625 million. Wormhole was 325 million. Those chains had audits. They had bug bounties. They had budgets for security that dwarf anything Hive has ever committed to.

Hive has the DHF and a handful of witnesses reading each other's PRs. Calling that a security strategy would be generous.

## What should happen

The point of this is to get ahead of something that is coming fast, not to assign blame after the fact. There are concrete things the Hive community can do right now that would genuinely move the needle.

Fund a proper chain audit through the DHF. Not a branding exercise. A real one, scoped at the consensus and signing code, done by a firm that has handled Graphene derived chains before. Budget six figures if that is what it takes. It is cheaper than a single successful attack.

Set up a bug bounty with real payouts. Immunefi tier numbers, not 100 HIVE for a critical. If you want security researchers to look at your chain, you have to pay them what they can get elsewhere.

Shameful plug, but I actually built a Hive based bounty app already called Hive Bounty where we could fund bounties already: https://hivebounty.com

Get the layer 2s audited separately. Hive Engine is running serious value through a JavaScript codebase that, to my knowledge, has never been through a formal review. Magi is activating. All of those need scrutiny.

Start running AI assisted code review now, while the models are still behaving themselves. Claude Code, Codex, whichever you prefer. Have them systematically walk the codebase. Every AI finding goes through a human reviewer, but the coverage you get from agentic review is already better than what most small OSS projects have today.

## Last thought

The era of powerful AI models is not coming. It is here. Mythos found a bug in OpenBSD that predates Bitcoin by nine years. Spud is sitting in a training cluster somewhere waiting for a release window.

Hive is a small chain with a small core team and a lot of legacy code nobody has looked at properly in years. The attackers will have access to the same tools as the defenders within 18 months, and unlike the defenders, they do not have to fill out an access request form.

If you are a witness, a dev, a stakeholder, or just somebody who cares about this ecosystem surviving the next cycle, start pushing for this now. Before Spud ships. Before the open weights catch up. Before someone runs Mythos Lite against the Hive daemon on a Tuesday and decides to see what happens.

The clock started last week.

One of the many things I've been chipping away at over the past months is the event badges. Each badge carries a QR code that does a few things at once: it onboards brand new users to Hive in a genuinely simple way, and it gives attendees everything they need on-site. They can find the full event timetable, a one-tap link to our local HOD Telegram group, and direct access to the @ecency Discord server. Seven months. No team. No funding. No one to share the load with.


![th199](https://hivepostify.cloud/uploads/posts/10969694a15bb98f3afb4b7fd5330cb6.webp)


Just me, a laptop, countless sleepless nights, and one belief that has never left me: **creators deserve to be paid for every single view they earn, not just the ones that happen within seven days.**

Today, I want to share something I have quietly started building. When it launches, it will change how every creator on this platform earns permanently.

**I have begun development on the HivePostify Monetization System.**

This is not just a plan. Work has already started. I am announcing it today because this community has stood behind me since the very beginning, and you deserve to know where this platform is going before it gets there.

---

## The Problem Every Hive Creator Knows

You spend hours writing an article. You publish it. For seven days, it earns rewards. Then it stops.

It does not matter if that article gets read ten thousand more times after those seven days. It does not matter if someone finds it a year later and shares it with their entire audience. The earning window is closed. The content keeps giving, but the creator stops receiving.

I have thought about this problem for a long time. I am building the solution directly into HivePostify.

---

## What the HivePostify Monetization System Will Do

### Ads That Respect the User

Ads will be displayed across the platform on articles, on videos, and on profile pages. But I am not building a platform that bombards users with pop-ups and interruptions. Every ad placement will be chosen carefully so that it feels natural within the experience. The reader keeps reading. The viewer keeps watching. The creator keeps earning. Nobody gets annoyed.

Gambling will never be promoted through HivePostify ads. This is a permanent policy. This platform exists for creators, freelancers, learners, and communities. The advertising environment will always reflect those values.

### Almost All Revenue Goes to the Creator

The vast majority of ad revenue generated from a creator's content will go directly to that creator. HivePostify is not a platform that quietly takes most of what you earned and gives you a small percentage. You built the audience. You created the content. You deserve to be paid for it.

Earnings will be paid in **AHPT**, HivePostify's native token, with instant withdrawal available. No waiting. No complicated processes.

### Lifetime Earnings Not a 7-Day Window

This is the part that matters most.

Every view a creator's articles and videos receive today, next month, next year, five years from now will count toward their earnings. A post published six months ago that still attracts readers every single day will still generate income daily. There is no closing window. There is no expiry date on your work.

**You create once. You earn forever.**

### A Dashboard That Shows You Everything

I will build a dedicated earnings dashboard for every creator on HivePostify. It will show total lifetime views across all content, earnings broken down per article and per video, full withdrawal history, and current balance all in one place, all transparent, all honest.

No confusion. No hidden numbers. Just a clear picture of what your content has earned and what you are owed.

---

## Videos Are Coming to HivePostify

Before the monetization system fully launches, I plan to bring video support to HivePostify both short-form and long-form.

Video is where attention lives today. It is also where ad revenue is strongest, meaning video creators on HivePostify will have significant earning opportunities from day one. Video hosting requires server infrastructure that I am actively working toward as this platform grows. The direction is set. The intention is firm.

Short videos. Long videos. Lifetime earnings on every view of every one of them.

---

## How Monetization Eligibility Will Work

Monetization will **not** be based on Hive reputation score.

I want to be clear about this because it matters. Reputation on Hive reflects how other users have voted on your content. It should not determine whether you can earn from your own work. A creator who builds a real audience, publishes genuine content, and attracts real views deserves to monetize regardless of their reputation number.

Eligibility will be based on real, measurable activity views, followers, and content engagement. Full criteria will be published in detail when the system is ready to launch.

---

## An Honest Note on Timing

My board exams are approaching. For the next several weeks, I need to dedicate more time to studying than coding. Development will continue, but at a slower pace. I would rather tell you this directly than go quiet and leave people wondering.

The moment my exams are finished, I will return to full-speed development. Monetization, video support, and every other update in the pipeline will accelerate from that point forward. Nothing is being abandoned. Everything is still being built.

---

## What This Means for You Right Now

If you are already publishing content on HivePostify, every article you post today is a permanent asset in your lifetime earnings record. When monetization launches, your existing content will already be part of your earning history. You are not starting from zero when the system goes live. You are already ahead.

If you have not started creating on HivePostify, the time is now before this platform gets crowded, before monetization launches, and before the earning system rewards those who were here early.

---

*Platform is live at hivepostify.cloud*  
*All activity verifiable on-chain at @hivepostify*  
*Built on Hive. Developed independently. One student. One mission.*

While using **HIVE READER MINI**, a friend recently asked me a very practical question:  
>👉 *How can I find the TXID of a deposit I made to an exchange (such as Binance)?*

This made me realize that although HIVE READER already supports viewing wallet records and account activities, **it didn’t display the TXID**, which can be inconvenient in certain scenarios.


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUUcd7YkQ9ekWcHZ1RoPCK3WuEExM2795yyH6WYdiSmkN/image.png)


When dealing with exchanges, **the TXID (transaction hash) is one of the most critical pieces of information**, as it allows the other party to quickly locate your transaction.

So, I’ve added this feature to HIVE READER MINI to make things easier for everyone 👇

---

## ✨ Key Update: Full TXID Display Support

You can now directly view the transaction ID (TXID) in:

- Wallet Activity  
- Activities  

---

## 🧩 Technical Improvements

This update goes beyond UI enhancements and includes backend optimizations:

- **Data Model Extension**  
  The Activity interface now includes a new `trx_id` field to store the transaction hash from the Hive blockchain.

- **Service Layer Optimization**  
  Updated the `getHistory` and `getWalletHistory` methods in `hiveService.ts`:  
  👉 Automatically extracts and stores the TXID for each operation when fetching account history from Hive nodes.


![ed2a96425f2c9b0588c48409855b3569.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWWJQmoYoyDQNDjt6DPhAoQs9NQrbEkxC2XJHKh9DEabG/ed2a96425f2c9b0588c48409855b3569.png)


## 🖥️ UI Enhancements: Clearer and More Intuitive

### 📌 JSON Modal Upgrade (JsonModal)

When you click the activity icon to view raw JSON data:

- If a TXID is present  
- It will be displayed prominently at the top of the modal in **orange text** under the **TXID** section

This makes it easy to spot at a glance.

---

## ⚡ New Feature: One-Click TXID Copy

To further improve usability, a quick copy feature has been added:

- 🆕 **Copy Button**  
  A small copy icon is now displayed next to the TXID

- ⚡ **One-Click Copy**  
  Click the icon to instantly copy the TXID to your clipboard

- ✅ **Visual Feedback**  
  The icon briefly changes to a checkmark (✔) to confirm a successful copy

- 🔄 **Independent State Management**  
  The TXID copy function works independently from the “Copy Full JSON” button for more precise interaction


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUQSsN373Gzr5ep93KNKThMrHaPnt2brBCXtJTwvQHzi7/image.png)


## 🚀 Practical Benefits

With TXID support, you can now:

- Quickly provide transaction proof to exchanges (e.g., Binance)  
- Easily look up transactions in Hive block explorers  
- Improve efficiency in troubleshooting and asset tracking  

---

## 🌐 Current Version

✅ **Version: v2.7.8**  
👉 https://reader.cutehive.com



We always listen to user feedback, and this update is a direct result of a real-world use case. We’ll continue refining and improving the tool to make it more practical and user-friendly.

**Step by step, contributing to the growth of the HIVE ecosystem.**

result.body:
I gonna call it day. But...

...in this blog post, I’d like to look back on the work I’ve done today – partly as a summary for myself, but also to show you all what I’ve managed to accomplish today! 

It’s now 10:30 p.m., and I started my work researching security vulnerabilities in the HIVE ecosystem around midday. First, I went through a few audits from last week to see if I’d missed anything, and I had something in mind that I’d been wanting to test for a long time. Namely, Witnesses can include a description along with their parameters for the blockchain, as well as a URL for their Witness announcement post or whatever—most use their profile or their project. And that’s exactly where I wanted to start and see what might happen—and yes, something did happen.


![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/ahM_AwIFbigAAAAC/dwight-schrute.gif)


I started by using my brother’s witness and entered various XSS payloads as URLs... from standard javascript:// to frontend-specific variables, I tried out about 50 different payloads and have to say—sure enough, the frontends I tested all passed with no significant errors! But I couldn’t just let that slide because there had to be something there—so I took my Claude subscription, threw everything I’d done so far out the window, and ran the AI through a bunch of different repos—because that’s the kind of work an AI can handle well. In the end, something interesting came out of it—namely, a pretty silly and simple error... In that very field, I could enter something specific and completely crash at least one frontend. The server behind it just said—Sorry, dude—something’s wrong here and threw me a 500 error. That was immediate confirmation for me, so I told the developer right away what was going on. He saw the problem right away and got to work on a fix. Less than 20 minutes later, the error was fixed and we were both happy :)


![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/HYGK4__zJFEAAAAC/thumbs-up-nice.gif)

---

But the day didn’t end there—since I don’t give up easily and, thanks to my years of experience, now know what matters when it comes to HIVE—I was able to use AI to identify additional vulnerabilities in HIVE frontends over the course of three cycles. In one of the vulnerabilities I found, the title wasn’t properly sanitized, making a stored XSS attack possible. The site operator fixed this immediately after I reported it.


![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/u2QCLfzxZnAAAAAC/nice-work-you-two-chief-li.gif)

---

I really don’t give up and keep going until I get tired or it no longer makes sense to pursue the goal—so I kept at it and found more stored XSS bugs—this time in an area I hadn’t really been focusing on, but which might still be used sometimes, and areas like that should be tested too. In this case, it was about looking at the history of a blog post and comparing two versions.
I reported it, and it was fixed right away. Perfect! I think I did a good job today (at least from my perspective) and made the Hive ecosystem a little bit more secure—even more secure than it already is!

![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/xTPo2esLHcMAAAAC/make-america-great-again-maga.gif)

---

That’s all from me for today—and for those wondering why I’ve already published five articles today: these are blog posts linked to a product on PeakD. You can support me and my work there every month by visiting my shop at https://peakd.com/@louis88/shop. But only if you like what I’m doing for the HIVE blockchain.

![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/3Y2EN-82AzwAAAAC/you-deserved-it-barney-ross.gif)

And for those wondering why Inleo’s Rafiki AI bot is so fascinated by the Flat Earth theory—well, that’s probably a topic for another episode titled “Security in the Hive Ecosystem with Louis and the Friendly AI Next Door” (who’s always happy to drop by for coffee).


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/EoKBea7Ni2Xf4j6wi6LY11Aj31y4Mrq4nwF57EUjRJtNxDAYyuXkuDvycm38CrC7GaX.png)


Well, with that in mind—see you next time, and sorry for all the spam today.

Cya

![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/zuLgj0hQlqIAAAAC/brrr-so-cold.gif)
